Proof. We use again the fact that all pipe dreams are obtained from the bottom pipe dream by ladder moves. Here, again all of the ladder moves we can perform are simple ladder moves that just move crossings along their diagonals. Two crossings in the same row of the bottom pipe dream can never slide past each other, and any two rows can slide independently by Lemma 3.6. Thus, row i contributes a factor hiL(i), and multiplying these factors gives us Sw = i hiL(i). □

blocks.text: Lemma 3.7. If w avoids 231 and 321, then Sw is a single CHM. In particular, Sw = hL(w). Proof. We use again the fact that all pipe dreams are obtained from the bottom pipe dream by ladder moves. Here, again all of the ladder moves we can perform are simple ladder moves that just move crossings along their diagonals. Two crossings in the same row of the bottom pipe dream can never slide past each other, and any two rows can slide independently by Lemma 3.6. Thus, row i contributes a factor hiL(i), and multiplying these factors gives us Sw = i hiL(i). □ Notice that, unlike the case of SEMs and analogously to the case for usual monomials, the maximal monomial in the CHM expansion of Sw is always hL(w). Finally, we prove that 321 and 231 avoidance are necessary conditions in order for Sw to be a CHM.
